text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Central Electoral Commission said that 31 parties and coalitions were going to contest in Bulgaria's general election due on April 19. Election campaign opened on Thursday.

-- A Bulgarian aircraft flying from Tirana to Sofia with 30 passengers of various nationalities on board on Thursday was the first plane to leave the Albanian airport since it was closed a week ago by armed unrest.
-- Bulgaria's state gas monopolist Bulgargas said it had cut off natural gas supplies to the country's biggest oil refinery Neftochim which had not paid its bills since last year.
-- Some 57 percent of Bulgarian army officers are supporting the country's bid for NATO membership, said Evgeni Georgiev, head of defence ministry's Center for Social Research.

-- The price of water for households and budget-funded non-profit organisations is expected to fall by some 20 percent on the average following a decision by the interim cabinet to change the pricing scheme for the energy used by water supply companies.
-- Some 73 percent of Bulgarians were living below the poverty line at the end of 1996, spending more than 40 percent of their income on food, the National Statistics Institute said.
-- Bulgaria will privatise six commercial banks by the end of 1998 under pledges made to international lenders, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said.
-- The European Court of Human Rights ruled that Bulgaria's former prime minister Andrei Lukanov was wrongly detained in 1992 on suspicion of misappropriating funds.
The court awarded Lukanov's widow and two children damages and legal costs after ruling unanimously that Bulgaria had violated Lukanov's rights to liberty and security.
-- Bulgaria's biggest commercial bank Bulbank posted 12.4 billion lev billion lev net profit for 1996, up from 788 million levs for 1955, the bank's chief executive director Chavdar Kanchev said.
